title: Speech capabilities and user benefits · Level 3
slo: Explain what speech recognition and speech synthesis do and how they support users.

exercises.question_text: Which are benefits of speech-enabled experiences? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Speech can reduce reliance on keyboards and screens. This enables hands-free operation.
Speech can be used while another task continues. This supports multitasking.
Speaking and hearing can feel conversational. This can make interactions more natural.
Speech does not eliminate the need for text alternatives. Some users prefer or require non-speech access.
options.better_fit: Speech-only interaction may fit a limited context, but not accessible general design.

feedback.intrinsic: Users needing text could lose access.
feedback.instructional: Speech expands choices; it should not remove text alternatives.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech can support hands-free work, multitasking, and natural interaction.

exercises.question_text: Which name also refers to speech synthesis?

options.rationale: Text-to-speech is another name for speech synthesis. Both convert written text into spoken audio.
Speech-to-text converts speech into written text. That process is speech recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: A written notice would not be spoken.

options.rationale: Audio capture records incoming sound. It does not generate spoken audio from text.
options.better_fit: It fits the first step of recognition.

options.rationale: Language modeling helps select likely word sequences. It is not the text-to-audio capability.

feedback.instructional: Use synthesis when text must be spoken aloud.

exercises.question_text: Speech recognition converts written text into spoken audio.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Recognition is speech-to-text; synthesis is text-to-speech.

exercises.explanation: Correct. That conversion is speech synthesis.

exercises.question_text: What does speech recognition do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Recognition takes spoken language as input. It begins with captured speech.
Producing written text from speech is recognition's core role. It is therefore called speech-to-text.
A transcription gives an app usable written content. That supports understanding a spoken request.
Reading text aloud is speech synthesis. Recognition moves from speech to text instead.

feedback.intrinsic: No written transcript would be produced.
feedback.instructional: Recognition listens and writes; synthesis speaks.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Recognition listens to speech and produces text.

exercises.question_text: Speech synthesis listens to spoken language and converts it into written text.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Synthesis starts with text and produces spoken audio.

exercises.explanation: Correct. That description belongs to speech recognition.

exercises.question_text: Which benefit helps an app reach global audiences?

options.rationale: Language and dialect support serves people in more places. This expands global reach.
Sampling rate affects audio detail. It does not add language or dialect support.

feedback.intrinsic: Unsupported language communities would remain excluded.
feedback.instructional: Global reach comes from language and dialect support.

options.rationale: Beam width balances recognition accuracy and latency. It does not expand language coverage.

feedback.intrinsic: A new language community would still be unsupported.
feedback.instructional: Choose supported languages and dialects for global reach.

options.rationale: Removing alternatives can create barriers. It does not improve global reach.

feedback.intrinsic: Some users could lose a usable output method.
feedback.instructional: Keep alternatives and support relevant languages and dialects.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Languages and regional dialects expand global reach.

exercises.question_text: Order the pieces into a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: State the spoken alert, then the TTS capability and the written information it delivers.

exercises.correct_answer: A spoken alert uses text-to-speech to deliver a written warning
exercises.explanation: Text-to-speech delivers written information as a spoken alert.

exercises.question_text: Speech capabilities include speech recognition and ___, which speaks written text aloud.

parts.text: Speech capabilities include speech recognition and

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The missing term would not name the spoken-output capability.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use speech synthesis for text becoming speech.

exercises.explanation: Speech synthesis, also called text-to-speech or TTS, converts text into spoken audio.

exercises.question_text: What is another name for speech recognition?

options.rationale: Speech recognition changes spoken language into written text. Speech-to-text names that direction.
Text-to-speech changes written text into audio. That is synthesis rather than recognition.
options.better_fit: It is another name for speech synthesis.

feedback.intrinsic: A spoken request would not be transcribed.

options.rationale: A neural vocoder generates audio waveforms in synthesis. It does not transcribe speech.
options.better_fit: It fits a waveform-generation stage of synthesis.

feedback.intrinsic: The needed written words would not appear.
feedback.instructional: Vocoding belongs to audio generation, not recognition.

options.rationale: Text normalization prepares written text for pronunciation. It does not convert speech into text.
options.better_fit: It fits a synthesis text-preparation stage.

feedback.intrinsic: The speaker's words would remain untranscribed.
feedback.instructional: Recognition starts with speech, not prepared written text.

exercises.question_text: Which users can speech accessibility support? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Synthesis can read written content aloud. This can support visual access needs.
Recognition can enable hands-free operation. This can support users with mobility challenges.
Audio alternatives can support reading disabilities such as dyslexia. Synthesis can provide that audio.
Accessibility supports a range of needs. Keyboard preference is only one reason to keep text alternatives.
options.better_fit: It fits one reason to provide text-based alternatives.

feedback.intrinsic: Many access needs would be ignored.
feedback.instructional: Design for visual, mobility, hearing, and reading needs while retaining alternatives.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Accessible speech design can support varied user needs.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The action and outcome no longer connect logically.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the feature, then state the capability and its written result.

exercises.correct_answer: A transcription feature uses speech recognition to create written call notes
exercises.explanation: A transcription feature uses recognition because recognition produces written text from speech.

exercises.question_text: Speech applications should meet ___ and provide text-based alternatives.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The accessibility requirement would be missed.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: WCAG is the accessibility guideline; TTS and MFCC are speech-related terms.

exercises.explanation: WCAG stands for Web Content Accessibility Guidelines and guides accessible experience design.
